vedic_reference.note: From Rigveda, Yajurveda, and Atharvaveda. सत्य (satya) means truth, and एन् (en) is a suffix used to form masculine nouns.

data.cultural_impact: The name Satyen holds immense values in the Hindu culture, representing honesty, morality, and righteousness. It is believed that a person named Satyen embodies these virtues and sets an example of truth and integrity for others to follow. In India, this name is widely used and revered, especially among families who place a high value on truth and morality.
data.spiritual_significance: Spiritually, the name Satyen represents one's commitment to living a truthful and virtuous life, which is a fundamental aspect of the Hindu dharma (moral code). The pursuit of truth is believed to bring inner peace and enlightenment, as well as bringing about harmony and balance in one's personal and professional relationships. Thus, the name Satyen symbolizes the individual's quest for self-realization and spiritual growth.

historical_references.reference: Satyen Chattopadhyay was a prominent Indian nationalist and a leader of the Indian National Congress during the late 19th and early 20th centuries.
historical_references.context: Satyen Chattopadhyay was born in 1873 in West Bengal, India, during the British Raj. He was educated in Calcutta and later became a prominent Indian nationalist leader. He played a key role in organizing the Quit India Movement in 1942, which demanded an end to British rule in India. Satyen Chattopadhyay passed away in 1945.

historical_references.reference: Satyavadhan Rao was a Maratha general who served under the Mughal Emperor Shah Jahan in the late 16th century.
historical_references.context: Satyavadhan Rao was born in the Maratha kingdom in western India. He rose to prominence as a military commander under the Mughal Emperor Shah Jahan. He led the Mughal forces against the Deccan Sultanate and played a key role in the Battle of Kalyan in 1616, which resulted in a decisive Mughal victory. Satyavadhan Rao passed away in 1632.
